  "text": "The first jar appeared in my refrigerator on Monday.

It contained a tooth and a handwritten label: APRIL.

I lived alone. April was my sister's name.

When I called her, she laughed, then stopped.

“I lost a crown this morning,” she said. “How did you know?”

I threw the jar into the building's rubbish chute.

On Tuesday it was back, beside a larger jar containing a wet pink crescent.

The label read: DANIEL.

My brother didn't answer. His wife told me he'd caught his ear in a machine at work.

I bought a padlock for the refrigerator.

Wednesday's jar stood on top of it.

Inside floated a small grey object I couldn't identify. The label bore my father's name.

He was still in surgery when I reached the hospital.

“Who told you?” the receptionist asked.

I stayed until morning. When I returned, every kitchen cupboard was open. Empty jars lined the shelves, each labelled with a name I knew.

At the back stood one tall enough to hold a man.

Its label was blank.

I packed a bag and called April from the car.

“Come here,” she said. “We'll figure it out.”

Behind her voice, glass clinked.

“What was that?”

“Nothing. Daniel brought some things over.”

I heard my brother ask whether she'd kept me on the line.

Then my father spoke, clearly, though the surgeon had said he wouldn't speak for weeks.

“Ask him where he is.”

I hung up.

In the rearview mirror, a strip of paper lay against the back window.

My name was written on it, facing inward.

The doors locked before I could reach the handle."
